description.narrative: Den föreslagna insatsen gäller en garanti till Impact Investment Exchange (IIX), för att täcka lån som ges ut under en obligation, Women's Livelyhood Bond No 6 (WLB6). Lånen ska användas till små- och medelstora företag för att öka kvinnors tillgång till kapital och främja kvinnors ekonomiska egenmakt. Omkring 30% av lånen förväntas också bidra till klimat- och/eller miljömässigt hållbar utveckling genom utlåning inom relevanta sektorer. Länder som berörs av insatsen är Kambodja, Indonesien, Indien, Vietnam och Kenya.

The proposed contribution concerns a guarantee to the Impact Investment Exchange (IIX), to cover loans issued under the Women's Livelyhood Bond No 6 (WLB6). The loans are to be used for small and medium-sized enterprises to increase women's access to capital and promote women's economic empowerment and transition into sustainable livelihoods. Around 30% of the loans are also expected to contribute to environmentally sustainable development through lending in relevant sectors. Countries covered by the proposed guarantee are Cambodia, Indonesia, India, Vietnam and Kenya.

The societal and economic consequences of the Covid-19 pandemic are not impacting everyone equally. In fact, the most vulnerable are also the hardest hit and pre-pandemic existing social and economic inequalities have now been exacerbated. The WLB6 aims to improve the economic empowerment of women (WEE) who face gender based discrimination that increases their likelihood of remaining low income or trapped in cycles of poverty. The guarantee will provide critical de-risking required to attract capital from bondholders that will then be deployed to a portfolio of women focused enterprises. Further, with approximately 30% of the WLB6 proceeds expected to be allocated to entities operating at the nexus of gender equality ("orange") and climate action ("green"), the contribution also aims to empower women as part of the solution to climate related challenges.
IIX is targeting an issuance size of ~US$100m that will compromise a multi-country and multi-sector portfolio of companies that will collectively empower women and girls to build economic resilience and advance climate action. The rationale behind the WLB Series is to help marginalized women borrowers to access capital, finance and assets, thereby improving livelihoods and increasing their financial resilience. The leverage of funding is expected to help women to reduce their carbon footprint and facilitate a just transition and to transform the financial system so that women, the environment, and under-served communities are given a value and a voice in the global market. IIX has specified the outcomes as follows:
Primary outcomes - Impacts on direct women clients: 1. Improved income generation ability (USD 200 000 000 250 000 000) 2. Improved financial resilience increased savings and income coverage (USD 2 900 000 3 000 000) 3. Improved productivity (water and sanitation) (USD 65 000 000 70 000 000) 4. Increased ownership of assets (USD 40 000 00041 000 000) 5. Improved climate action (USD 14 000 000 15 000 000)
Secondary outcomes: Impact on the family, the community, the state, and the planet: 1. Enhanced multi generational impact 2. Strengthened women, peace, and security agenda 3. Improved community and planetary resilience to environmental shocks and stresses
Tertiary outcomes: Impact on the Gender Lens Investing Movement and the Sustainable Finance Ecosystem: 1. Advancing the gender lens investment movement in line with the orange bond initiative a) Gender Positive Capital Allocation b) Gender lens capacity and diversity in leadership c) Transparency in investment process and reporting 2. Catalyzing the sustainable finance ecosystem (actors of common mission of building gender equal, climate resilient and sustainable financial markets)
Expected Outputs (Gender disaggregated matrix): 1. 170 000 women entrepreneurs receiving loans 2. 105 000 women clients availing of micro savings and micro insurance products 3. 20 00021 000 women clients receiving water and sanitation linked loans 4. 6 000 6500 women clients availing of affordable housing loans 5. 3000 3500 women benefiting from clean energy solutions

During 2025, the WLB6 portfolio-level impact performance remained within the expected range (/- 10% variance) for the number of women impacted and the Social Return on Investment (SROI: dollar value of social impact experienced by women impacted by WLB6 per dollar invested. It is a composite calculation of actual SROI from January 2024 to December 2025 and projected SROI til December 2027 (end of the bond tenor)): -165,106 women impacted against the target range of 152,600 -186,600. - SROI $3.81 against the target of $4.24
In terms of results from the proceeds connected to different SDG targets, the following is noted: ~163,376 women from lowincome communities were equipped to combat poverty through financial inclusion (SDG1) ~30,782 women smallholder farmers were supported with agricultural loans to maintain and improve their yields, and combat growing pressures due to environmental pressures (SDG 2) ~14,370 women and girls experienced improved health outcomes including reduced risk of exposure to waterborne communicable diseases (SDG 3) ~140,125 young women and girls benefited from financial support to stay longer in school (SDG 4) ~165,106 women were empowered to sustain their livelihoods and better combat genderbased discrimination, advancing women empowerment through financial inclusion (SDG 5) ~14,070 women benefited from improved access to clean water and sanitation facilities, saving ~2 hours per day and improving their productivity (SDG 6) ~5 women owned and/or women ed SMEs were provided access to clean and reliable energy sources (SDG 7) ~142,376 women were able to establish and maintain stable sources of income, including micro-entrepreneurs who were provided with affordable credit to sustain their businesses and women smallholder farmers involved in agri-value chains (SDG 8) US$100 million mobilized from developed countries towards emerging markets as official development assistance and foreign direct investment (SDG 10) ~530 women benefited from improved mobility and safety outcomes through access to affordable housing loans, leading to improved security and shelter outcomes (SDG 11) ~26,179 women empowered to build environmental resilience through access to clean energy (mitigation) and access to water or sustainable agricultural inputs (adaptation) (SDG 13) WLB6 coalesced a range of public and private sector partners: 2 placement agents, 6 law firms, and 1 guarantee partner (SDG 17)
Ahead of the Partner Meeting organized by the Embassy of Sweden in Bangkok on May 1819 2026, IIX submitted a note summarizing some key impact results generated from the partnership with Sida. This partnership then includes all three guarantee contribution (to WLB5, WLB6 and WLB7). While kept on a very overarching level, it gives a flavor of what type of impact the guarantees are contributing to:
"Partnership with Sida: Institutional Change and Capacity Strengthening Sidas partnership, alongside Global Affairs Canada, UNESCAP, and UNCDF, helped demonstrate that blended finance structures can mobilize institutional capital towards underserved women and enterprises in emerging markets. Through the WLB Series, Sidas support contributed to validating and scaling gender lens investing across multiple bond issuances and geographies, while supporting the broader growth of the Orange Movement, which has mobilized over US$1.5 billion globally. At the borrower level, the WLB Series strengthened ESG and governance practices through impact covenants and the IIX Values framework, which assesses portfolio companies against IRIS, GRI, IFC Performance Standards and the UN SDGs. Several borrowers subsequently formalized environmental and sustainability policies, strengthened board-level ESG oversight, and introduced antibribery and labour monitoring mechanisms. The partnership also strengthened transparency and accountability through semiannual impact reporting, independent secondparty verification, direct engagement with end borrowers through multilingual surveys and impact verification processes. All WLB issuances are independently assessed for compliance with both the Orange Bond Principles and ICMA Sustainability Bond Guidelines, strengthening credibility and consistency across the bond lifecycle. This reporting and verification infrastructure has contributed to stronger standards for impact measurement within gender lens investing and blended finance markets."
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
